briefs.headline: Pirates put up eight on Boston to take the finale 8-3
briefs.summary: Pittsburgh scored twice in the first and five in the third. Kirby Yates took the win at 1-5; Patrick Sandoval fell to 1-2. The Bucs are 61-65, 16.5 back in the Central.

briefs.headline: Miami score seven late and beat the Reds 7-1
briefs.summary: Cincinnati led early before Miami took two in the eighth and five in the ninth. Josh Ekness won at 1-1; Tejay Antone fell to 2-2. The Reds are 59-64.

sections.label: Around the Leagues

briefs.headline: Cameroon beat Malawi 3-0 for a first WAFCON title
briefs.summary: Marie Ngah scored in the 20th and first-half stoppage time and Naomi Eto in the 30th, in Rabat. Cameroon had lost three previous finals; Malawi were ranked 153rd and making their debut.

briefs.headline: Manchester City accept a 65.4M pound bid for Rodri
briefs.summary: The 2024 Ballon d'Or winner, 30, has agreed a four-year deal with Barcelona after seven seasons and 298 appearances at City. He missed Sunday's 3-0 Community Shield loss to Arsenal after minor back surgery.

sections.note: MLB played a full Sunday card and none of it moved a division: Milwaukee lead the Central at 77-48, five clear of the Cubs. Sunday's NFL preseason and MLS results were available only from aggregators this desk does not cite.

notes.item: Bluefish is five per day from a for-hire vessel but three per day for private recreational anglers, which is the number that applies to most of this readership.
Flounder is closed in North Carolina coastal waters and unlawful to possess. Topsail Sound is coastal water, so Marine Fisheries governs it, not the inland digest.
Nothing else opens within two weeks. The first general season is squirrel on Sept. 12, with a youth weekend Sept. 5-6.
Goose, duck, dove, woodcock and snipe dates are not in the summary table. They come from a separate WVDNR migratory bird publication issued in August, and HIP registration is required.

sections.label: On the Water

waters.read: 4620 cfs - blown out. Stay on the bank.
waters.working: Up from 179 cfs and 2.00 feet a day ago, so nothing is fishable and nothing is wadeable. The pocket water and plunge pools that are the whole river in August are gone under. As it drops the seams along the undercut banks clear first, and that is where a heavy stonefly nymph and a sculpin pattern go in.

waters.near: 14 miles above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.read: 28.0 ft and rising - up and pushing. Expect colour and current; fish the slack behind anything solid.
waters.working: Up nearly three feet in a day and coloured, so the fish are off the main current. Shad are the forage: work a white swimbait through the slack behind the wing dams and the barge cuts rather than the open channel.

waters.near: below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.read: 30.8 ft and rising - up and pushing. Expect colour and current; fish the slack behind anything solid.
waters.working: Also up nearly three feet. The lock wall and the riprap are the holding water while it is pushing; a crawfish-coloured crankbait tight to the rock is the second look after the swimbait.

waters.reading: Sound highs 12:08 AM and 12:43 PM at Hampstead; lows 6:32 AM and 7:05 PM.
waters.read: Fish the moving water either side of high at 12:08 AM and 12:43 PM in the sound.
waters.working: Tide first: the 12:43 p.m. high is the one daylight window, and the push into it and the fall behind it are the hours. Mud minnows, shrimp and finger mullet are the forage, so work the grass edges and the oyster bars while the water is moving.
waters.note: Hampstead is the sound station and is the read that matters; the oceanfront station at Ocean City Beach pier runs over an hour ahead and is quoted only for a surf read. No water temperature is carried today - the Wrightsville Beach gauge returned none.

sections.note: USGS does not gauge the Ohio at R.C. Byrd, and the Corps tailwater data is not reachable from this pipeline. The two gauges above are the ones that bracket the dam, and neither is the tailwater.

kicker: Two of the 14 followed teams played Sunday, and the Williams River is unfishable at 4620 cfs.
